## Summary

Add an OSS-aligned **diff-coverage** signal on the Gerrit Verified lane (epic
`5664-b797-60b9-49ef` / soupy-bilineate-whiteeye, story S4): report line coverage on the lines a
change touches, reusing the coverage data the primary Ubuntu cell already collects. This is the
epic's chosen coverage improvement in place of raising the blunt global branch-coverage floor
(deferred in research 81fd because targeted mutation testing is the stronger oracle).

## Context / Problem

`_build-and-test.yml`'s default-suite step already collects in-process coverage on exactly one
cell (ubuntu-latest + py3.13) via `--cov=rebar --cov-report=term-missing:skip-covered`, but that
data is only rendered as a terminal report and a whole-tree `fail_under` floor
(`[tool.coverage.report]`, pyproject). Mainstream Python OSS additionally reports coverage on the
**changed lines** of each change, so a change that adds under-tested lines is visible even when
the global floor still passes. rebar had no such signal.

## Approach

Two edits, both on the coverage-bearing cell only, adding **no new job and no new test run**
because they reuse the coverage run that already happens:

1. **Emit `coverage.xml`.** Extend the existing conditional coverage-flag expression on the
   ubuntu+3.13 cell in the default-suite `pytest` step to also pass
   `--cov-report=xml:coverage.xml`. pytest-cov writes the XML from the same session. The flags
   stay gated to `!startsWith(matrix.os, 'macos') && matrix.python-version == '3.13'`, so no
   other cell changes.

   The exact `diff-cover` flag spellings were confirmed empirically against the installed
   tool's `--help` before landing: `--compare-branch` accepts a commit-ish (`HEAD^`, not only a
   branch), and `--fail-under`, `--format markdown:<path>`, and the positional coverage-file arg
   all resolve — so a wrong-flag silent no-op (which `|| true` would otherwise mask) is ruled out.

2. **Add a report-only `diff-cover` step** after the default-suite step, guarded to the same
   ubuntu+3.13 predicate. Diff-coverage is a **pre-merge** signal, and rebar's pre-merge lane is
   Gerrit, so the step runs only on the **Gerrit Verified lane** (`inputs.gerrit-refspec` set):
   - on the post-merge push/branch lane it **skips** with a `::notice::` — that lane has no
     proposed diff (the change is already in main) and its `actions/checkout` is shallow with no
     `origin/main` tracking ref, so there is no reliable base to compare against;
   - on the Gerrit lane it installs `diff-cover` ad hoc with `uv pip install` into the same
     `.venv` (a report tool, kept out of the lock — the exact pattern the pip-audit step uses);
   - it compares against the patchset's **parent** (`HEAD^`), deepening by one first
     (`git fetch --deepen=1`) because a shallow patchset checkout has no parent object — the same
     technique the pip-audit dependency-map gate uses;
   - it runs `diff-cover coverage.xml --compare-branch='HEAD^' --fail-under=0 --format
     markdown:"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"` — strictly **report-only** (`--fail-under=0` plus a `|| true`
     belt), writing the changed-line coverage into the job step summary (the `--format markdown:`
     spelling is the non-deprecated form; `--markdown-report` warns and is slated for removal);
   - it guards on `coverage.xml` presence (skips with a `::notice::` if a patchset predates the
     step), and routes the refspec through an `env:` var (`GERRIT_REFSPEC`) rather than direct
     `${{ }}` interpolation into the run block, satisfying zizmor's template-injection audit.

**Non-blocking by design:** a diff-coverage dip is surfaced to the author, never a merge gate.
The enforcing coverage check remains the whole-tree `fail_under` floor. Because the Verified gate
binds this workflow from trusted main, the new step first executes against the NEXT change's
patchset after this one lands — that is the live-validation path.

## Parity contract

`tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` pins the coverage-flag expression by exact string in
three embeddings: the `_COVERAGE_FLAGS` constant, its regex in `_coverage_flags_by_cell`, and —
**twice** in `_render_default_suite_body` (the match key AND the returned resolved value, which
otherwise raises `AssertionError('unrendered workflow expression')`). All are updated to include
`--cov-report=xml:coverage.xml`. The new diff-cover step is neither the `default` nor the
`integration` tier, so `test_matrix_keeps_every_test_tier_but_collects_coverage_once` continues to
pass unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The ubuntu+3.13 default-suite `pytest` invocation emits `coverage.xml` via
      `--cov-report=xml:coverage.xml`, with the flags still gated to that one cell (verifiable by
      inspecting the `test` job's coverage expression in `_build-and-test.yml`).
- [x] A report-only `diff-cover` step runs on ubuntu+3.13 **only when a Gerrit refspec is set**,
      compares against `HEAD^`, and never fails the job (`--fail-under=0`); on the non-Gerrit lane
      it exits 0 with a skip notice (verifiable by reading the step's `run` block).
- [x] The refspec is env-routed (no direct `${{ }}` interpolation in the run block) and
      `make lint` (ruff + format + complexity baseline + zizmor over the 7 vote-path workflows +
      actionlint) exits 0.
- [x] `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` passes (29 tests) with the updated
      `_COVERAGE_FLAGS` across all three embeddings.
- [x] No new CI job and no second test run are added: the change is one extra `--cov-report`
      reporter on the already-running coverage session plus one cell-gated report step
      (verifiable by diffing the `test` job — no new matrix cell, no new `uses:`/job).
